newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't defends value placed on CVRD.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't defends value placed on CVRD.

text.p: The Brazilian government on Monday said it would not reconsider the price set for the sale of shares in Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), the state-owned mining concern.
The government said the value placed on CVRD last week was a fair reflection of the company's worth.

Presidential spokesman Sergio Amaral said the government was advised by two independent consultants before setting a valuation of 10.4 billion reais ($9.96 billion) for the company, which is on track to be privatized next month.
"President (Fernando Henrique Cardoso) sees no reason for that price to be reconsidered," Amaral told reporters.
"Vale's privatization is being carried out using all the necessary technical considerations so that the process moves forward normally and causes no problems to the country as a whole," he said.

Newspapers on Monday published extracts of a confidential report produced by professors from the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ) who valued CVRD's total assets at $12 billion. The report said government officials underestimated the true value of Vale's mineral holdings, including its gold and uranium reserves, in an attempt to speed up the sale.
After months of delays, the Brazilian government last week set a minimum price of 26.67 reais for Vale do Rio Doce shares.
The government is planning to auction an initial 45 percent of the company's voting shares on April 29 in what is being billed as the biggest privatization ever held in Latin America.
The remaining 51 percent of the Brazilian government's stake will be offered later to employees and floated in Brazil and overseas.
